title: Design at the Speed of Adjectives — Paul Bakaus, Renaissance Geek, Inc.
talk_summary: Paul Bakaus describes 'impeccable', a design skill that compresses design vocabulary (adjectives/verbs like 'bolder', 'quieter', 'distill', 'harden') into agent instructions with project-specific definitions, so agents steer toward intended outcomes instead of inventing their own interpretation. The core mechanism is a shared, defined vocabulary plus multi-shot iteration at the right altitude of control, explicitly rejecting one-shot automation.

takeaways.technique: Defined-vocabulary skill files (adjectives with explicit semantics)
takeaways.what_they_do: Each steering word (e.g. 'bolder') is backed by a skill file that defines what it means in-context and what it must NOT do, so the model stops inventing its own interpretation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: An adjective with nothing behind is just a nicer prompt. So, you really have to tell the agent what you mean by the word that you're using.

takeaways.what_they_do: The skill instructs the agent to show its work and ask whether a human would believe the change was made; the agent then reflects and self-corrects.
takeaways.evidence_quote: show someone your work and say AI make this bolder made this bolder if they believe you you failed

takeaways.technique: Map workflow and define injection points before building tooling
takeaways.what_they_do: Before building, he maps the non-linear workflow of the target user and identifies where human/agent control should be injected at each stage.
takeaways.evidence_quote: whenever I build a tool, I actually map the workflow first... what are the injection points along that route

takeaways.technique: Right-altitude control (avoid too-low and fully-autonomous extremes)
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues against both pixel-level micromanagement and fully agentic one-shot; pick the altitude of instruction that matches the task stage.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there's this middle ground that we haven't explored enough like what is the exact level of control?

takeaways.technique: Reject auto-mode; keep human steering in the loop
takeaways.what_they_do: Explicitly refuses to ship an 'auto' mode that picks commands itself, because the value is in steering, not one-shotting.
takeaways.evidence_quote: There is no auto and there will be no auto in my opinion
